text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; can you tell me exactly how long you have been experiencing this swelling and if the pain worsens with activity or rest?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pseudotumor (Giant Cell Tumor of Tendon Sheath) is unlikely given the age and genetic history; the clinical picture of a young boy with spontaneous knee swelling and a family history of similar issues strongly suggests a genetic disorder such as Hemophilia (specifically Hemophilia A or B) presenting with a hemarthrosis, though a spontaneous fracture or a rare genetic skeletal dysplasia like Cleidocranial Dysplasia affecting the joints should also be considered. I will now request specific tests.
